title: Staged schema negotiation and deferred-tool-retry acceptance checklist
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Define acceptance criteria for a staged schema negotiation protocol + deferred tool-invocation/retry semantics across streaming outputs. We need deterministic client-visible objects even when partial frames are emitted, tools are rate-limited, or gateway auth/queueing delays occur. This ticket captures criteria, test cases, and operational observability requirements so engineering can implement a predictable runtime behavior and product teams can validate acceptance.
scope_changes: Original PRD assumed immediate, synchronous tool invocation on first eligible 'function call' frame. Scope updated to: 1) add configurable deferred-invoke window (0-12s) during which the model can emit additional context; 2) introduce an explicit 'schema-commit' frame that finalizes object shape; 3) require idempotency tokens and signed commit anchors for Private deployments; 4) add gateway-level retry budgets and circuit-breaker signals; 5) add telemetry events for each negotiation phase.
decision_log: 1) Streaming frame model: adopt three frame classes (proto, delta, commit). 2) Tools accept 'deferred' flag + idempotency-key; gateway returns commit-ack. 3) Retry semantics: exponential backoff bounded by per-request retry budget; on budget exhaustion return structured fallback object with error classification. 4) For ephemeral auth delays, gateway may 'defer' execution and mark frames with a deferred_until timestamp. 5) Private deployments: idempotency tokens must be KMS-signed per security request.
acceptance_criteria: Frame semantics: Stream contains zero or more 'proto' frames (schema hints), zero or more 'delta' frames (partial fields), and a single 'commit' frame that finalizes schema. Clients must be able to validate and accept the object after 'commit'.
Commit idempotency: Every commit frame carries an idempotency-key (UUID v4). Replaying the same commit-key must be recognized by tool proxies and produce an identical commit-ack without side effects.

Deferred-invoke window: When model emits a 'deferred' flag on a function/tool call, runtime will wait up to configured window (default 5s) for supplementary context before invoking the tool. If additional context arrives, it must be included in the tool input; if window expires, tool is invoked with collected context.

Retry budget: Gateway maintains a per-request retry budget (default 3 attempts). Retries on 429/503 use exponential backoff starting at 200ms, capped at 2s, and stop when budget exhausted. Exhaustion triggers emission of a 'tool-fallback' commit object with structured error code and remediation hints.

Observability: Emit telemetry events for phases: negotiation.start, negotiation.proto_received, negotiation.delta_received, negotiation.commit_sent, tool.defer.start, tool.invoke.attempt, tool.invoke.success, tool.invoke.retry, tool.invoke.fallback. Each event must include request_id, commit_key, and latency_ms.

Backpressure and circuit-breaker: If gateway-level queue latency exceeds threshold (configurable), runtime must emit a 'deferred' advisory to client and mark subsequent commit frames with backpressure=true. Circuit-breaker tripping must be visible in Console (route-level metric).

Fallback object shape: When tool invocation fails permanently, runtime must return a well-formed JSON object matching the committed schema with a top-level field 'tool_error' containing {code, reason, retryable:false|true, partial:false|true}. This preserves consumer contracts.

Streaming correctness: Clients reconstructing the object from proto+delta+commit must be able to validate against the final schema without external heuristics. Tests must cover out-of-order delta arrival (network reordering) and duplicate deltas.
Security: For Private deployments, idempotency keys must be signed with customer KMS and verified by tool proxies. Any unsigned commit must be rejected with a 401 and logged to audit.
Latency SLO impact: Enabling deferred-invoke window must not increase median end-to-end commit latency by more than 10% for P95-sensitive routes; track via new 'negotiation_latency_ms' metric.
test_plan: Unit tests: frame encoder/decoder handles proto/delta/commit, assigns sequence numbers, rejects malformed frames.
Integration test: model-client -> runtime -> gateway -> tool proxy flow with deferred window set to 3s; assert tool receives aggregated context when additional deltas arrive within window.
Idempotency test: replay same commit_key multiple times and assert single tool side-effect and identical commit-ack responses.
Chaos test: inject 429/503 from tool proxy, validate retry budget honored, backoff behavior observed, and structured fallback emitted after exhaustion.
Reordering test: deliberately shuffle delta frames; ensure final assembled object equals expected canonical object after commit.
Security test: submit unsigned commit to Private deployment; expect 401 and audit event.
Performance test: enable deferred window in a synthetic workload and measure negotiation_latency_ms across 10k requests; confirm <=10% regression at median.

E2E consumer test: sample client SDK consuming streamed frames should expose a simple API: onSchema(proto), onUpdate(delta), onCommit(object) and receive final typed object even when fallback occurred (tool_error present).
rollout_notes: Phase 1 (canary): runtime feature gated. Enable staged negotiation on 5% of traffic for non-critical routes only. Monitor negotiation.start and commit_sent events.
Phase 2 (beta): increase to 25%, enable retry budget telemetry and tool.invoke.retry counters in Console.
Phase 3: enable by default, publish migration guide for clients on how to handle proto/delta/commit frames and consume tool_error fields.
Migration tip: clients that only support single JSON emission should subscribe to onCommit and ignore proto/delta frames until commit arrives.
Rollback plan: expose runtime flag to disable 'deferred' handling; on rollback, system will invoke tools immediately and emit a compatibility-warning metric.
